chunks: From him, from Ṣafwān, from al-ʿĪṣ ibn al-Qāsim, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who urinated in a place where there was no water, so he wiped his private part with a stone, and his private part and thighs had perspired. He said: «He washes his private part and his thighs.» And I asked him about one who wiped his private part with his hand, then his hand perspired and touched his garment—should he wash his garment? He said: «No.»
ai.seo_question: Does sweat transfer impurity after cleaning urine with a stone in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about impurity transfer after cleaning oneself with a stone when water is unavailable. It distinguishes between moisture affecting the private part and thighs, which requires washing, and perspiration from the hand after wiping, which does not require washing the garment.
